intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: by the time this episode drops Tuesday morning, Forever character creation and name reservation open at 1 p.m. Pacific, class tuning lands with maintenance, and the Fabled Kindo'jan deadline closes with that same maintenance.
rundown: the WoW: Forever beta wrapping up with a send-off party, and what name reservation looks like
Blizzard reversing course and adding an RP-PvP ruleset for launch
a first real look at Forever's endgame: three raids on December 9 and nine new dungeons
Midnight's next patch, Echoes of the Worldcore, hitting the PTR
class tuning for October 27, with Subtlety Rogue getting rolled back
one more week for the Fabled Kindo'jan achievement
the Liadrin story backlash we didn't get to last week
and we'll close out the news with Fortune's Xbox report, BioWare closing its doors, and a crowded November launch calendar

items.title: The Forever Beta Is Over: Name Reservation Opens October 27
items.synopsis: Forever's five-week beta closed October 23 with a send-off party, and the next stop is character creation and name reservation on October 27.
points: the beta closing October 23 after five weeks of playtesting
the final day turning the starting zones into a party, with Stitches crashing Goldshire and Super Hogger in Elwynn
big crowds in Stormwind and Thunder Bluff for the send-off, and nothing from the beta carrying over
Blizzard spending a few days on priority issues and server work before launch

points.text: character creation and name reservation opening Tuesday, October 27, running through November 3
points.sub: NA opens at 1:00 p.m. PDT, EU at 18:00 CET

points: up to three characters total across every ruleset, so two on PvP leaves you one for Normal or RP
pre-purchase required: the Skyborne Heroic or Epic Pack, or the Warcraft Forever Collection
names first come, first served, so have a backup ready
the End of Beta Special, episode 5 of the Forever Podcast, with Aggrend, Clay Stone, Ana Resendez and Michael Nuthals
launch still set for November 4
questions: Did either of you get on for the send-off, and what was the best moment of the beta for you?
Three characters across every ruleset: how are you splitting yours?

items.title: Blizzard Reverses Course: Forever Gets an RP-PvP Ruleset
items.synopsis: Days after raising concerns on their own podcast, Blizzard decided to add a Roleplay-PvP ruleset for launch on November 4.
points: the original lineup at announcement: Normal, PvP, Roleplay and Hardcore, with no RP-PvP
the devs talking through their concerns with an RP-PvP ruleset on the Forever Podcast
Blizzard on October 22: we've carefully examined what it would take to add it to WoW Forever and decided to go for it
the RP-PvP ruleset arriving with launch on November 4
Blizzard working to have it selectable for name reservations on October 27
the rulesets article updated the same day with how they all work
no grouping across rulesets, and no free hopping between them
collections and Legacy Points account-wide, with Hardcore coming after launch
a fast, public reversal driven by player feedback, two weeks before launch
questions: Does a fast reversal like this make you trust the Forever team more, or worry about what else could change?
Would either of you roll RP-PvP, or is it Normal and PvP for us?

items.title: Forever's Endgame: Three Raids on December 9, Nine New Dungeons
items.synopsis: Blizzard laid out Forever's first raids, all unlocking December 9, and the nine new dungeons you'll level through on the way.
points: Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair all unlocking December 9 for level 60
the Barrow Deeps: 10 players, 8 bosses, in the prison that held Illidan for 10,000 years
entrances to the Barrow Deeps from Mount Hyjal, Winterspring and Blackmaw Hold
Hyjal Summit: 20 players, 13 bosses, opening with a battle against an ancient guardian, then branching paths
Onyxia's Lair: 40 players, a three-phase fight, and you'll want fire resistance

points.text: Onyxia attunement coming back: the Drakefire Amulet, through a faction questline
points.sub: it runs through Upper Blackrock Spire; the amulet only has to be in your bags

points: nine new five-player dungeons from level 13 to 60
Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site, City of Dalaran, The Drowned City and Krol'dok Stronghold
then Alcaz Prison, Blackmaw Hold and Shaper's Terrace in Kalimdor
raids landing five weeks after launch, so the first month is a leveling and dungeons race
questions: Ten, twenty and forty: which raid size do you want our group to start with?
Five weeks from launch to raids. Enough time to get the guild to 60 and attuned?

items.title: Next Up for Midnight: Echoes of the Worldcore on the PTR
items.category: World of Warcraft: Midnight, Patch 12.1.7 PTR
items.synopsis: Midnight's next content update is on the PTR, sending us back to Dornogal with a new campaign, new Lorewalking and more Omnium Folio runes.
points: the new campaign, The Return to Dornogal: Xal'atath has breached the Worldcore
Arator, Brinthe, Dagran and Brann working out how to get through the damaged Coreway
the Singularity motion comic on October 23, Arator's Void story setting up the patch
new Lorewalking with Li Li Stormstout: Jaina, Thrall, the Titans and Tyr

points.text: Talebound, a new solo-or-group mode with its own cosmetics store
points.sub: it wasn't open on the PTR yet as of mid-October

points: Turbulent Timeways for eight weeks, with the Markeet of the Infinite skyriding mount
two more Omnium Folio runes, Empowerment and Critical Mass, plus two more Motes of Omnial Inquiry
a PTR bug-fix build on October 22
no release date yet, and Blizzard Watch guessing early December
questions: Back to Dornogal and Brann again: are you excited for this story, or ready to leave Khaz Algar behind?
If 12.1.7 lands right as Forever raids open, which one gets your time?

items.title: Class Tuning October 27: Subtlety Rolled Back
items.category: World of Warcraft: Midnight, Class Tuning
items.synopsis: Tuning lands with maintenance on October 27, and Subtlety Rogue gives back a big chunk of the buff it got in 12.1.5.
points: Subtlety Rogue taking an 8% cut to all ability damage

points.text: the devs: the 12.1.5 compensation buff overshot expectations, so they're rolling back a significant portion of it
points.sub: and since the patch helped Trickster more than Deathstalker, Trickster's Fazed drops to 5% (was 7%)

points: that's after Subtlety got 14% more ability damage in 12.1.5
Fire Mage getting 5% more damage in PvE, and 5% less in PvP for overperforming
Resto Druid getting dungeon help: Verdancy +60%, Regrowth +10%, Improved Swiftmend up to 40%
Feral up 5%, plus Marksmanship AoE buffs to Trick Shots, Explosive Shot and Volley
Affliction's Unstable Affliction and Destruction's Rain of Fire both up 20%
San'layn Vampiric Strike cut 20% in PvP
the October 20 hotfixes uncapping Conquest and Bloody Tokens
Spoils of War on: 50% more Conquest and 40% more Honor in battlegrounds and arenas
questions: Fair rollback, or did Subtlety players just get the rug pulled two weeks after a buff?
Does uncapped Conquest plus Spoils of War get either of you back into PvP this season?

items.title: Labyrinth Follow-Up: Fabled Kindo'jan Extended a Week
items.category: World of Warcraft: Midnight, Labyrinth of Kindo'jan
items.synopsis: Blizzard owned up to the Labyrinth's buggy first week and gave everyone one more week at the Fabled Kindo'jan achievement.
points: Blizzard acknowledging that first-week bugs blocked Labyrinth runs, including Fabled Let Me Solo Him: Kindo'jan
Blizzard saying they've now addressed the vast majority of those bugs
the deadline moving to weekly maintenance on October 27
a follow-up to last week's rough first week: falling through floors, missing boss credit, stuck scenarios
the October 21 fix: talk to Kinduru in the antechamber to leave mid-scenario
Jan'alai Tear now stacking to 4, and shorter characters no longer falling through Jan'alai's Refuge
by the time this episode is out, that window has closed
questions: Did either of you get Fabled Kindo'jan done in the extra week?
Is a one-week extension enough of a make-good after a week like that?

items.title: Liadrin's Send-Off: The Backlash Keeps Going
items.synopsis: We didn't get to it last week: the Kith'ix finale ends Lady Liadrin's story, and a week later players are still unhappy with how it was handled.
points: spoiler warning before we start this one
Liadrin channeling the Light against Kith'ix, then collapsing after the fight
her last words: Darkness will never prevail
Icy Veins calling it one of the most unceremonious, anticlimactic deaths in WoW history
Windows Central: the most painfully, miserably weak writing in all of Blizzard
the common complaint: little build-up for a character around since The Burning Crusade
a death in a .5 patch, cut off from the main story
part of a pattern players are tired of: old feuds getting settled too easily
GameSpot on October 19: Forever is soaring, but Midnight is struggling
still no public Blizzard response that we could find, and fans guessing she comes back as Forsaken
questions: Did Liadrin's death land for you, or did it feel rushed?
Is the faster patch schedule hurting the story, or is this just how WoW does character deaths now?

items.title: Fortune's Xbox Report, and EA Closes BioWare
items.synopsis: Fortune reports more Xbox cuts and a $1,200-plus console under Asha Sharma, and EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next Mass Effect.

points.text: Fortune's report on Asha Sharma's Xbox: 1,868 jobs cut so far toward a 3,200 target
points.sub: mostly unnamed sources, so this is reported, not confirmed

points: more rounds reportedly planned for November and January
Game Pass being rebuilt into tiers you pick à la carte
a handheld for holiday 2027, and the next console for holiday 2028 projected at $1,200 to $1,800
former Blizzard president Mike Ybarra: a console at that price will never sell
staff talking about a sale or spinoff, which Microsoft disputes on the record
BioWare's farewell message on October 21: the studio is closing and the next Mass Effect is cancelled
around 400 EA jobs cut, about 50 of them at BioWare, after EA's $55 billion buyout closed in August
Dragon Age: The Veilguard reaching about 1.5 million players, nearly 50% under EA's target
EA keeping the Mass Effect IP, so any future game comes from another studio
questions: Would either of you buy an $1,800 Xbox, or does that number end the console for you?
BioWare gone after 30 years: what's the BioWare game that meant the most to you?

items.title: The Launch Calendar Around Forever: MW4, Zelda, GTA VI
items.synopsis: Forever launches into the most crowded November in years, with Zelda the next day and GTA VI two weeks later.
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 already out since October 23 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Switch 2
Xbox going all in on MW4, down to ads taking over custom dashboard backgrounds
WoW: Forever launching November 4

points.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a full remake for Switch 2, out November 5, one day after Forever
points.sub: voiced cutscenes, 60 FPS, a jump button; $59.99 digital, $69.99 physical

points: a Zelda-themed Switch 2 landing October 29
Rockstar's GTA VI launch trailer out October 23, with the game arriving November 19
Forever's raids opening December 9, right after all of it
questions: What's actually pulling you away from Forever in November: Zelda, GTA, or nothing?
Does GTA VI two weeks in hurt Forever's first month, or is the WoW crowd locked in?
